To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we used cyclostratigraphy to construct a 405-kyrs floating astronomical time scale to date the GSSP of the basal Guzhangian Stage, and that our results indicate that the Earth–Moon distances and the length of day were different in the middle Cambrian compared to the present.
the cyclostratigraphy, astronomical time scale, and paleogeophysical parameters of the Luoyixi GSSP of the Guzhang Stage were established.

we constructed a floating astronomical time scale using the stable 1.4 Ma eccentricity cycles for the Guzhanian Stage, the Earth–Moon system was more compact and the length of day was shorter during the middle Cambarian (500 Ma) compared to present day.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cyclostratigraphy and astronomical time scale of the Luoyixi Section, which provides a basis for further high-resolution time scale studies of the Cambrian.
the development of a high-precision time scale for the Guzangian Stage and provides a basis for further research into the Cambrian Period.
the cyclostratigraphy, astronomical calibration and astronomical parameters of the GSSP for the Guzhanigian Stage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Luoyixi GSSP of the Guzhang Stage is dated at 501.1 ± 0,8 Ma.
the Guzhang Stage was deposited over 1.4 Ma (from 501.1 to 499.7 Ma).
the Cambrian Period lasted for 56.5 ± 2.5 Ma (from the end of the Ediacaran Period at 542 Ma to the base of the Ordovician System at 486 Ma).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cyclostratigraphy can be used to provide a reliable time scale for the Cambrian, and the obtained fundamental obliquities can be used to estimate the length of day, the Earth–Moon distances, and the eccentricity of the Earth’s orbit during the Cambrian Period.

(1) The Luoyixia section is a high-resolution time reference for the Guzangian Stage, (2) the 405-ky eccentricity cycles were recorded in the middle Cambrian strata, and (3) the length of day was longer and the Earth–Moon distances were shorter than the present day values during the Cambrian Period.

the cyclostratigraphy and astronomical calibration of the GSSP for the Guzhanigan Stage provide an accurate time scale for the middle Cambrian, which is important for the understanding of the evolution of life and climate change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cyclostratigraphy can be used to constrain a floating astronomical time scale for the Cambrian.

a high-resolution time framework for the Guzlangian Stage has been developed, and that this time framework can be applied to other sections in order to improve the correlation and chronostratigraphy of other Cambrian stages.
the 405-kyrscale can be used to date the Cambrian Period and that it can be applied to the other Phanerozoicoic periods to construct a high-resolution time-scale.
